title: Lattice 2-group symmetries: operators, defects, and gauging
authors: Lucas Z. Brito, Salvatore D. Pace
abstract: We construct and study lattice realizations of finite 2-group symmetries in ${2+1}$d quantum lattice systems with finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. We focus on two broad classes of 2-groups with 0-form symmetry group $G$ and 1-form symmetry group $A$: split 2-groups with trivial Postnikov class ${[β]\in\mathcal{H}^3(G,A)}$, and central 2-groups with trivial action ${ρ\colon G\to\text{Aut}(A)}$. In both cases, we construct symmetry operators on the full tensor-product Hilbert space that become 2-group symmetry operators when restricted to the topological subspace of the lattice $A$ 1-form symmetry. While the lattice split 2-group symmetry operators are onsite, the lattice central 2-group symmetry operators are not, and can only be made onsite after introducing ancillae. We extensively explore various manifestations of $ρ$ and $[β]$ for these lattice 2-group symmetry operators and demonstrate their agreement with expectations from quantum field theory. These manifestations arise in the transformation of operators carrying symmetry charge, the structure of lattice 2-group symmetry defects, and the dual fusion 2-category symmetries obtained by gauging the lattice 2-group symmetries. We further propose families of local symmetric Hamiltonians for both classes of lattice 2-group symmetries and identify exactly solvable limits lying in phases with spontaneous 2-group symmetry breaking and nontrivial symmetry-enriched topological order. In one such limit, the gauged Hamiltonians are exactly solvable lattice realizations of the corresponding 2-group gauge theories, whose ground-state degeneracies we calculate.
summary: This theoretical work develops a framework to realize finite 2-group symmetries on quantum lattice models in 2+1 dimensions. By constructing symmetry operators and proposing local Hamiltonians, the authors connect abstract algebraic structures (like 2-groups) to concrete physical models exhibiting topological order. This provides powerful tools for characterizing and solving complex strongly correlated quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper constructs and studies lattice realizations of finite 2-group symmetries in $2+1$d quantum lattice systems.
main_result: It demonstrates that symmetry operators for split and central 2-groups can be constructed, leading to proposals for local symmetric Hamiltonians and identifying exactly solvable limits realizing 2-group gauge theories.
method: The authors use advanced algebraic techniques involving cohomology, cocycle conditions, and the construction of symmetry operators on tensor-product Hilbert spaces.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum lattice models (QLMs) in $2+1$ dimensions defined on a lattice, characterized by finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: Symmetry operators, symmetry defects, ground-state degeneracies, and the structure of the dual fusion 2-category.
important_parameters: The structure of the 2-group (split vs. central), the Postnikov class $[ eta]$, and the lattice geometry (e.g., triangular lattice).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to QLMs with tensor-product Hilbert spaces, which limits the realization of true topological operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the defect interpretation of symmetry actions ($ho$ and $[ eta]$) and the branching structure of the underlying simplicial complex.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses split 2-group symmetry, then central 2-group symmetry, followed by discussions on the mathematical structure of the symmetries, and concluding with proposals for symmetric Hamiltonians and solvable limits.
why_interesting: The deep connection between higher symmetries (2-groups) and the construction of exactly solvable, symmetry-protected topological phases is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum matter states.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Defect interpretation in 2 + 1d of the action ρ and Postnikov class [β] of the 2-group (1.3). (a) The action ρ causes an a ∈A topological defect line to become a ρg(a) topological defect line when penetrating a g ∈G topological defect surface. (b) The Postnikov class [β] determines how a topological defect line can end on a 0-dimensional junction of three G topological defect surfaces.

Figure 2: We consider quantum lattice systems whose spatial lattice is a triangular lattice. There is a corresponding simplicial complex whose branching structure is displayed here. Namely, the orientation of each link always points upwards and to the right.

Figure 3: The Postnikov class [β] of a 2-group symmetry modifies the 0-form symmetry operator algebra in the presence of a 0-form symmetry defect. In the k-defect sector, multiplying CG(k) ≤G symmetry operators creates a 1-form symmetry operator according to the slant product ιkβ.

Figure 4: Gauging web of 2-group symmetry operators in field theory. In the split 2-group case, gauging the 1-form A-symmetry leads to a dual semidirect product 0-form G ⋉ˆA-symmetry for ˆA = Hom(A, U(1)). In the central 2-group case, gauging the 1-form A-symmetry leads to a direct product 0-form G × ˆA-symmetry with mixed anomaly depending on [β]. Gauging the 0-form G symmetry in both cases leads to a dual 2 Rep G symmetry.
